newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin says may cut tax when deficit nil.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin says may cut tax when deficit nil.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin on Friday said he would be open to the idea of cutting taxes once Canada's federal deficit is eliminated.

"Absolutely ... when we have eliminated the deficit, we will obviosly be open, for the first time, to be making a lot of very important series of choices which are going to involve tax cuts, which are going to involve spending in building the economy." Martin told reporters during a breakfast with members of the National Press Gallery.
He said his government would be implementing selective tax cuts even before the deficit is brought down to zero.

Although he admitted that the country's unemployment rate, which has hovered around 10.0 percent in the past six months, is a cause of concern, Martin stopped short of pledging any new government job creation measures in his next budget.
The budget is expected to be released some time in February next year.
In remarks that bore resemblance to a campaign speech, Martin said the next elections would focus around the federal government's direct involvement in managing the country's affairs.

"I believe that if not the "over-theme" of the next election campaign, certainly the subliminal theme of the next election campaign is going to be the role of government: whether Canadians want an activist government or not," Martin said. ((Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau, 613-235-6745))
